title: Sphere mapping spaces preserve weak homotopy equivalences
statement: Use k-spaces and the k-space topology from [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits], and continuous based homotopy groups and path components from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a continuous map of topological spaces inducing a bijection on path components and isomorphisms of all positive homotopy groups at every basepoint. For $r\geq0$ put $S^r=\{v\in\mathbb R^{r+1}:\|v\|=1\}$ and put $S^{-1}=\varnothing$. For every integer $r\geq-1$, postcomposition induces a weak homotopy equivalence $k\operatorname{Cont}(S^r,X)\to k\operatorname{Cont}(S^r,Y)$. Here $\operatorname{Cont}(K,Z)$ carries the compact-open topology generated by $[L,U]=\{h:h(L)\subseteq U\}$ for compact $L\subseteq K$ and open $U\subseteq Z$, and weak homotopy equivalence means the same bijection and based-group isomorphisms as for $f$.

source.place: Lemma 2.4.17, printed pp. 56-57; Proposition 2.4.22(1) for kification. The lemma is stated for compact-open mapping spaces in Top; kification leaves all compact-Hausdorff sphere/cube tests unchanged. No Stacks tag is claimed.

proof.text: Write $Z^K=k\operatorname{Cont}(K,Z)$ for the compact disks and spheres used below. First reduce arbitrary $X,Y$ to k-spaces without adding a hypothesis. By the final-topology definition in [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits], for any compact Hausdorff $A$ a map $A\to Z$ is continuous exactly when the same map $A\to kZ$ is: for every k-open $U$, continuity of the first map gives that its inverse image is open, and the reverse follows from continuity of $kZ\to Z$. Thus kification preserves the paths, based cubes and cube homotopies defining all homotopy groups in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and $kf$ has the same component and group maps as $f$. For compact Hausdorff $A,K$, their product is compact Hausdorff. Applying [lem-coef-compact-open-currying] to $A\times K$ shows that $\operatorname{Cont}(K,kZ)$ and $\operatorname{Cont}(K,Z)$ have the same continuous maps from every such $A$. Their underlying sets agree by taking $A$ to be a point; hence their final k-topologies agree. Consequently $(kZ)^K=Z^K$ canonically. We may therefore prove the assertion with $X,Y$ k-spaces, using kified limits as specified by the realization node.

source.place: Hovey, Model Categories, Lemmas 2.4.13–2.4.17, printed pp. 55–57; Definition 2.4.21 and Proposition 2.4.22(1), printed pp. 57–58. Explicit cubical, retraction and low-degree expansions by the worker.

proof.text: The compact-open formulas used below are continuous by [lem-coef-compact-open-currying]; the sphere and disk sources are locally compact Hausdorff. Fixed precomposition and postcomposition are also continuous directly: the inverse image of a subbasic $[L,U]$ is respectively $[g(L),U]$ or $[L,h^{-1}(U)]$. After kification these formulas remain continuous, since their composites with compact Hausdorff test maps are continuous. For each $m\geq0$, restriction $q_Z:Z^{D^m}\to Z^{S^{m-1}}$ is a Serre fibration, with no model-category theorem used. Indeed, a disk-parameter lifting problem, by currying, prescribes a continuous map on $D^a\times((D^m\times\{0\})\cup(S^{m-1}\times I))$. This union is a retract of $D^m\times I$: for $v\in D^m$ and $t\in I$ put $s=1/\max(1-t/2,\|v\|)$ and $R(v,t)=(sv,2+s(t-2))$. The denominator is at least $1/2$. The formula is continuous, lands either on the bottom or on the side, and fixes both (on either subset $s=1$). Compose the prescribed map with $1_{D^a}\times R$ and curry back to obtain the lift. The initial glued map is continuous by pasting over the two closed subsets. For $m=0$, $S^{-1}$ is empty and the same formula retracts the point-cylinder onto its bottom. This establishes the defining lifting property for every $a\geq0$.

source.place: Hovey, Model Categories, Lemmas 2.4.13–2.4.17, printed pp. 55–57; Definition 2.4.21 and Proposition 2.4.22(1), printed pp. 57–58. Explicit cubical, retraction and low-degree expansions by the worker.

proof.text: For all $m\geq0$, first work with the compact-open space $\operatorname{Cont}(D^m,Z)$ before kification. Let $e_Z:\operatorname{Cont}(D^m,Z)\to Z$ be evaluation at $0$ and $c_Z:Z\to\operatorname{Cont}(D^m,Z)$ the constant-map section, so $e_Zc_Z=1_Z$. By the evaluation clause of [lem-coef-compact-open-currying] (with $A=\operatorname{Cont}(D^m,Z)$, $K=D^m$ locally compact and $g$ the identity), $\operatorname{ev}:\operatorname{Cont}(D^m,Z)\times D^m\to Z$ is continuous; hence $e_Z$ is continuous, and $c_Z$ is continuous as the transpose of the projection $Z\times D^m\to Z$. Define $H:\operatorname{Cont}(D^m,Z)\times[0,1]\to\operatorname{Cont}(D^m,Z)$ by $H(h,t)(v)=h(tv)$. It is the transpose, by the first clause of [lem-coef-compact-open-currying] with $A=\operatorname{Cont}(D^m,Z)\times[0,1]$ in the product topology, of the continuous map $((h,t),v)\mapsto\operatorname{ev}(h,tv)$; so $H$ is continuous, with $H(h,0)=c_Ze_Z(h)$ and $H(h,1)=h$. With the constant homotopy $K(z,t)=z$ on $Z$, [lem-coef-homotopy-equivalence-weak] applies to $f=e_Z$, $g=c_Z$ (its homotopies need not fix basepoints): $e_Z$ induces a bijection on path components and group isomorphisms $\pi_n(\operatorname{Cont}(D^m,Z),h)\to\pi_n(Z,h(0))$ for every $h$ and $n\geq1$, with the cubical conventions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. By step 1, passing to the kification $Z^{D^m}=k\operatorname{Cont}(D^m,Z)$ changes none of the paths, based cubes or cube homotopies (all have compact Hausdorff sources), so the same holds for $e_Z:Z^{D^m}\to Z$. Since $e_Yf^{D^m}=fe_X$, the maps $f^{D^m}$ are bijective on components and induce all based-group isomorphisms, composing these isomorphisms with the given maps of $f$.

source.place: Hovey, Model Categories, Lemmas 2.4.13–2.4.17, printed pp. 55–57; Definition 2.4.21 and Proposition 2.4.22(1), printed pp. 57–58. Explicit cubical, retraction and low-degree expansions by the worker.

proof.text: Induct on $r\geq-1$. At $r=-1$ both mapping spaces are singletons. For $r\geq0$, assume the assertion for $r-1$. The sphere is the pushout $D^r\amalg_{S^{r-1}}\{*\}$. When $r=0$ this is the two-point space. When $r\geq1$, collapse the disk boundary to the marked point of $S^r$; in polar coordinates $v=tu$, the quotient map is $(\sin(\pi t)u,\cos(\pi t))$, with the boundary sent to the south pole. This is continuous also at $t=0$, is bijective away from the collapsed boundary, and identifies the compact quotient homeomorphically with the Hausdorff sphere. By currying, a continuous parameter family of sphere maps is exactly a compatible disk family and point family. More explicitly, for a compact Hausdorff parameter $A$ the map $A\times(D^r\amalg\{*\})\to A\times S^r$ is a continuous surjection from a compact space to a Hausdorff space, hence closed and quotient: images of closed subsets are compact and therefore closed. The compatible disk and point adjoints descend through this quotient and are continuous. This description includes $r=0$, where both points are needed for surjectivity. The final k-topology and the limit description in [lem-coef-realization-finite-limits] therefore give $Z^{S^r}=Z^{D^r}\times_{Z^{S^{r-1}}}Z$, where $Z\to Z^{S^{r-1}}$ is the constant map. Projection $p_Z:Z^{S^r}\to Z$ is evaluation at the marked point. It is a Serre fibration: a lifting problem projects to the disk-restriction problem of step 2, and its lift together with the prescribed point family is a lift in this pullback.

source.place: Hovey, Model Categories, Lemmas 2.4.13–2.4.17, printed pp. 55–57; Definition 2.4.21 and Proposition 2.4.22(1), printed pp. 57–58. Explicit cubical, retraction and low-degree expansions by the worker.

proof.text: Fix $x\in X$ and put $y=f(x)$. Let $F_X(x)=p_X^{-1}(x)$ and $F_Y(y)=p_Y^{-1}(y)$, with the kified fibre topologies. These are also the fibres of $q_X:X^{D^r}\to X^{S^{r-1}}$ and $q_Y$ over the constant boundary maps at $x,y$. For $r\geq1$, paths in these fibres correspond, by [lem-coef-compact-open-currying], exactly to homotopies of disk maps fixed on their boundary. Thus $\pi_0F_X(x)=\pi_r(X,x)$ and $\pi_0F_Y(y)=\pi_r(Y,y)$ naturally, as sets. This agrees with the cube convention of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]: the radial homeomorphism from $[-1,1]^r$ to $D^r$ sends $v\ne0$ to $(\|v\|_\infty/\|v\|_2)v$, has inverse $w\mapsto(\|w\|_2/\|w\|_\infty)w$, and extends at zero; both carry boundary to boundary. If $r=0$, a based map from the two-point $S^0$ is determined by its value at the other point, so $F_X(x)=X$ and $F_Y(y)=Y$. In every case $F_X(x)\to F_Y(y)$ is a bijection on path components, using respectively the given $\pi_r(f,x)$ or $\pi_0(f)$.

source.place: Hovey, Model Categories, Lemmas 2.4.13–2.4.17, printed pp. 55–57; Definition 2.4.21 and Proposition 2.4.22(1), printed pp. 57–58. Explicit cubical, retraction and low-degree expansions by the worker.

proof.text: We now prove that this fibre map induces all positive homotopy-group isomorphisms, at every $\alpha\in F_X(x)$. Apply the natural long exact sequences of [lem-coef-serre-homotopy-exact-sequence] to the restriction fibrations $q_X,q_Y$, with basepoints the disk map representing $\alpha$ and its image. The maps of total spaces $X^{D^r}\to Y^{D^r}$ are isomorphisms on positive groups by step 3, and those of bases $X^{S^{r-1}}\to Y^{S^{r-1}}$ by induction. For completeness the group chase on $\pi_{j+1}E\to\pi_{j+1}B\xrightarrow{\partial}\pi_jF\to\pi_jE\to\pi_jB$, $j\geq1$, is as follows. To lift $u'\in\pi_jF'$, lift its image in $E'$ to $E$. Its image in $B$ vanishes by injectivity on $B$, so choose $u\in\pi_jF$ over it. The difference between $u'$ and the image of $u$ is a boundary from $B'$; lift that class from $B$ and multiply $u$ by its boundary. For injectivity, a class $u$ killed in $F'$ maps to zero in $E$, so is a boundary of $b\in\pi_{j+1}B$. The image of $b$ in $B'$ comes from $\pi_{j+1}E'$; lift this element from $E$ and divide $b$ by its image. The resulting class is zero by injectivity on $B$, hence $u=0$. Products rather than subtraction give the identical chase when $j=1$. This proves the required fibre isomorphisms; together with step 5 the fibre maps are weak homotopy equivalences.

source.place: Hovey, Model Categories, Lemmas 2.4.13–2.4.17, printed pp. 55–57; Definition 2.4.21 and Proposition 2.4.22(1), printed pp. 57–58. Explicit cubical, retraction and low-degree expansions by the worker.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-serre-homotopy-exact-sequence] a second time, now to evaluation $p_X,p_Y$ and a basepoint $\alpha\in X^{S^r}$ with $x=\alpha(*)$. The maps on bases are the original isomorphisms of $f$, and those on fibres are step 6's isomorphisms and step 5's component bijection. Here is the total-space group chase, including $j=1$. To lift $a'\in\pi_j(Y^{S^r},f\alpha)$, lift its base image to $b\in\pi_j(X,x)$. Its boundary is trivial because its image is trivial in $\pi_{j-1}F_Y$ and the fibre comparison is injective (a pointed-set injection when $j=1$). Exactness supplies $a\in\pi_j(X^{S^r},\alpha)$ over $b$. The difference between $a'$ and the image of $a$ lies in the image of $\pi_jF_Y$; lift it from $\pi_jF_X$ and correct $a$. For injectivity, a killed $a$ has trivial base image by injectivity on the base, hence comes from $u\in\pi_jF_X$. Its image in $F_Y$ is a boundary from $\pi_{j+1}Y$. Lift that base class from $\pi_{j+1}X$ and divide $u$ by its boundary. Injectivity on $\pi_jF$ makes the remainder trivial, and the boundary maps trivially in the total group. Thus $a=0$. This proves the based-group isomorphisms for all $j\geq1$ and all $\alpha$.

source.place: Hovey, Model Categories, Lemmas 2.4.13–2.4.17, printed pp. 55–57; Definition 2.4.21 and Proposition 2.4.22(1), printed pp. 57–58. Explicit cubical, retraction and low-degree expansions by the worker.

proof.text: It remains to prove the component bijection, without assuming connected spaces or silently applying a group five lemma to pointed sets. For each $x\in X$, using the constant sphere maps as the compatible total-space basepoints, [lem-coef-serre-homotopy-exact-sequence] identifies the components of $X^{S^r}$ mapping into the component of $x$ with the orbit set of the action of $\pi_1(X,x)$ on $\pi_0F_X(x)$. The corresponding description holds for $Y$ at $f(x)$, and the comparison is equivariant. The acting-group map is an isomorphism by the hypothesis on $f$, and the fibre-set map is bijective by step 5. Therefore the orbit-set map is bijective: lift any representative for surjectivity; if two lifted representatives become equivalent, lift the group element witnessing that equivalence and use injectivity of the set map. Finally $\pi_0X\to\pi_0Y$ is bijective, so these bijections over base components assemble to a bijection on all components of the sphere mapping spaces. Every evaluation fibre is nonempty because it contains the constant map; if $X$ is empty, $Y$ is empty by the component hypothesis, and all nonempty-sphere mapping spaces are empty. This completes the induction and, by step 1, proves the original assertion for arbitrary spaces and every $r\geq-1$.
